text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for hypertension (high blood pressure) include heart-healthy lifestyle changes and first-line prescription medications tailored to your readings and overall health risks.
snippet_highlighted_words: heart-healthy lifestyle changes and first-line prescription medications

list.snippet: DASH Diet: Eat a diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while avoiding saturated fats.
Sodium Reduction: Limit salt intake to under 1,500 to 2,000 milligrams per day to reduce fluid retention.
Regular Exercise: Engage in regular aerobic exercise, like brisk walking, for 30 minutes most days.
Weight Management: Lose excess weight and maintain a healthy body mass index (BMI).
Limit Alcohol and Quit Smoking: Reduce alcohol consumption and avoid tobacco products.

text_blocks.snippet: When lifestyle changes are not enough—or for stage 2 hypertension—doctors often prescribe one or more of these classes of blood pressure drugs from the American Heart Association guidelines:

list.snippet: Thiazide Diuretics: Water pills like hydrochlorothiazide that help the body get rid of excess sodium and water.
ACE Inhibitors: Drugs like lisinopril that relax and widen blood vessels.
ARBs (Angiotensin Receptor Blockers): Medications like losartan that block hormones causing blood vessels to constrict.
Calcium Channel Blockers: Drugs like amlodipine that prevent calcium from entering muscle cells in the heart and blood vessels to lower resistance.

text_blocks.snippet: If you share your recent blood pressure readings or any other medical conditions (like diabetes or kidney disease), I can provide more tailored information on which treatment paths doctors typically prioritize.
